Every night, too many Americans go to sleep without shelter or a place to call home. Congress must take action to address this growing problem.

https://t.co/4KQFspmzvf
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) provides food benefits to low-income families. We must strengthen and protect this program. #AskAdam https://t.co/2wj1i5RX6M

From disability services, nutrition assistance, family planning services, and caregiver programs, there are so many tools available to families in Washington. 

Navigating these programs can be hard, but https://t.co/O8EMeVJVnl is a good place to start: https://t.co/MXa0vC4Qam

MAGA Republicans are willing to shut down the government if they don't get what they want: harmful cuts to Social Security, K-12 education, nutrition assistance for kids, and more.

That's unacceptable. We need to pass government funding bills and prevent a Republican shutdown.

Today is the launch of the CARE Department, a new type of crisis response that will divert mental health, substance-use disorder, and wellness-related calls to a new trauma-informed support center. 
https://t.co/6qGrJtmync

By diverting mental health, substance use disorder, and wellness-related calls to specialized service providers, the CARE Department will help reduce the strain on police departments and connect individuals in crisis with the services they need. https://t.co/NbJebzeeWW

It’s possible to get healthy, fresh, and free food throughout Washington state. Whether you’re looking for hot meals, nutrition assistance, or groceries, you can learn more here: 
https://t.co/ic9gFKFL8B

Got to visit the Cowlitz Tribe in Tukwila today. I heard about their incredible work with individuals struggling with substance use disorder. The Cowlitz Tribe has been operating a Medication Assisted Treatment van to provide health care access in rural and urban communities. https://t.co/9tAyDZrw0A

The MAT van allows them to bring substance use disorder treatment directly to people who need it. I helped secure $1 million in federal funding in FY23 to support their health services. Learn more: https://t.co/mf12EyptYo

Thank you @RepGwenMoore for sharing your personal story with food insecurity.

Rep. Moore's story is just one example of why we must protect nutrition assistance programs that so many parents use to support their families.

Today is National Native HIV/AIDS Awareness Day, a day to promote HIV testing, prevention, and treatment in American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian communities.

We can help #StopHIVTogether by reducing the stigma. https://t.co/lLLoexzPpX

May is Mental Health Awareness Month. This month is an opportunity for us to have honest conversations about mental health, reduce the stigma associated with mental health diagnoses, and advocate for treatment and recovery options. 
https://t.co/ff7eDdD6n6 https://t.co/5PstJyNVEP

AANHPI communities have some of the lowest mental health care utilization rates in the United States. In 2021, only 25% of Asian adults w/ a mental illness received treatment.

During #AANHPIMonth & #MentalHealthAwarenessMonth, its crucial we promote awareness of this disparity.

I've requested $3M in federal funding to help King County Water District 54 modernize their water treatment processes. This District serves the drinking water needs of over 5,000 residents. A new treatment system will help remove manganese, iron, and other contaminants. https://t.co/FFqUMAWjze

Today is National Voter Registration Day! Thank you to those who laid the path for universal voting rights. I recommend you all exercise your civic duties and check your voter registration today. https://t.co/AFTJd3SOgJ

Each person’s mental health is unique and requires individualized care. By providing tailored services, effective treatment is possible. I was glad to visit @SoundMH Health Clinic today and continue the important conversation around mental health. https://t.co/h54gCGJEpH

Today’s Wear Red Day, where we Go Red to save women’s lives to raise awareness for heart attack and stroke symptoms. Pay attention to your health and the wellbeing of your loved ones today and throughout the month.
Women and children cannot access nutrition programs, which puts their health and safety at risk. This includes 4.5 million children under the age of five just within the Congo alone.

Two months ago, Army veteran Scott Olson was hired by the VA. Kent's Scott Olson had previously received cancer treatment at the Seattle VA and knew the importance of the VA’s work.

But, last week, Olson was unexpectedly fired via email because of Donald Trump and Elon Musk. 

DOGE’s mass layoffs have devastated hundreds of Washingtonians, just like Olson, across many federal agencies. 

The President’s cuts to the VA jeopardize lifesaving care and are a slap in the face to Washington’s veterans. https://t.co/5BQUQe2ukh

With more affordable housing, access to mental health services, and ability to seek drug treatment, we can address the homelessness crisis in King County. Those on the local level need to stop governing through experience and govern effectively.

King County's Department of Community and Human Service is losing $1.4 million in funding for substance abuse treatment and mental health services at the hands of the Trump administration. Eight programs will be hit by these cuts, including crisis hotlines and substance abuse counseling for teenagers. This costs jobs and puts thousands of lives at risk. The President is putting tax cuts for billionaires over the wellbeing of our neighbors in Washington. https://t.co/P29pWc8P3N
I heard from Ron Patterson, a University of Washington professor living with Stage 4 Prostate Cancer, about how proposed cuts to the NIH will impact his treatment. https://t.co/1AmZf1OQin

In May, we recognize Mental Health Awareness Month, a time for us to have real conversations about our mental health to reduce the stigma around these diagnoses.

Having publicly spoken about my anxiety, I can personally attest that exploring treatment options helped me find strategies to manage my mental health.

More than one in five adults have a mental health condition, yet care remains unaffordable and inaccessible. We need more pathways to treatment and support year-round. Recovery is possible and our nation needs to help out all that are fighting.

House Republicans voted yesterday to cut $300 billion from food assistance for hungry children and seniors over the next 10 years. This budget slashes SNAP benefits and will take food away from working people to fund tax breaks for billionaires.
https://t.co/PEhJijh6jJ

Having gone through my own struggles with anxiety, I wanted to speak about the importance of recognizing May as Mental Health Awareness Month. Treatment is possible and it does get better, so I encourage you all to put your health first. https://t.co/Wq9Y3JJFLb
